rawFindings.title: Case-sensitive RegExp routes collide in the base-route cache
rawFindings.explanation: The cache key is lower-cased whenever the app router is not case-sensitive. That setting applies to string paths, but RegExp paths keep their own case sensitivity. As a result, distinct regex routes such as `/abc/` and `/ABC/` get the same cache key and the second method is attached to the first route's regex.
rawFindings.suggestion: Only apply the router case-sensitivity lower-casing to string paths, or include the original RegExp string/flags without lower-casing for RegExp paths.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With default settings: `app.get(/abc/, getHandler); app.post(/ABC/, postHandler);` then `POST /ABC` incorrectly returns 404 because the POST handler was attached to the existing `/abc/` route instead of a new `/ABC/` route.
